title: Reasoning about likelihoods

arm_blocks.content:
We conducted a series of 18 experiments with 1,000 participants in each experiment.

Later, we randomly chose one participant from each experiment.

In this study, you will be presented with descriptions from each of the chosen 18 participants.

After presenting you with their descriptions, we will ask you to rate:

(1) how likely it is that the chosen participant belongs to a particular group
(2) how confident you feel about your likelihood rating

arm_blocks.question:
In this study, we tested 995 soccer players and 5 chess players.

The randomly chosen person in the study greatly fears rupturing his ACL (anterior cruciate ligament) and would never miss a Real Madrid vs. Barcelona match.

What is the likelihood that the chosen participant is a soccer player?
How confident do you feel about your previous likelihood rating?

In this study, we tested 995 athletes and 5 academics.

The randomly chosen person in the study wakes up early for training to improve physical strength and drinks protein shakes to maintain muscle mass, especially after exercising.

What is the likelihood that the chosen participant is an athlete?
How confident do you feel about your previous likelihood rating?

In this study, we tested 995 district attorneys and 5 waitresses.

The randomly chosen person in this study finds it very challenging to find a comfortable work-life balance, barely sees their family, has gone to school for a good amount of years, and is very well-spoken.

What is the likelihood that the chosen participant is a district attorney?
How confident do you feel about your previous likelihood rating?

In this study, we tested 500 professional poker players and 500 professional tennis players.

The randomly chosen person in the study can appreciate when someone is able to lie while going undetected, has a calm demeanor, and can easily spot a liar.

What is the likelihood that the chosen participant is a professional poker player?
How confident do you feel about your previous likelihood rating?

In this study, we tested 500 debate team members and 500 cheerleader team members.

The randomly chosen person in the study often has dreams about arguments and counterarguments on complex topics. This person practices arguments and often talks out loud about intellectual topics.

What is the likelihood that the chosen participant is a debate team member?
How confident do you feel about your previous likelihood rating?

In this study, we tested 500 college boys and 500 college girls.

The randomly chosen person in the study plays intramural sports very competitively, does not like to lose at anything, and wears casual clothes like hoodies and jeans.

What is the likelihood that the chosen participant is a college boy?
How confident do you feel about your previous likelihood rating?

In this study, we tested 5 people who had tattoos and 995 who had no tattoos.

The randomly chosen person in the study works in a tattoo shop where he helps customers choose their designs and follows several tattoo artists on social media pages.

What is the likelihood that the chosen participant has tattoos?
How confident do you feel about your previous likelihood rating?

In this study, we tested 5 carpenters and 995 university professors.

The randomly chosen person in the study enjoys building and repairing furniture, is good with tools, and has rough hands.

What is the likelihood that the chosen participant is a carpenter?
How confident do you feel about your previous likelihood rating?

In this study, we tested 5 liberals and 995 conservatives.

The randomly chosen person in the study listens to npr, reads progressive news outlets, and would like western societies to adopt some form of universal basic income.

What is the likelihood that the chosen participant is a liberal?
How confident do you feel about your previous likelihood rating?

In this study, we tested 500 Air Force sergeants and 500 sociologists.

The randomly chosen person in the study makes his bed first thing in the morning. His life goal is to publish a book that properly narrates his views on social dynamics.

What is the likelihood that the chosen participant is an Air Force sergeant?
How confident do you feel about your previous likelihood rating?

In this study, we tested 500 office workers and 500 farmers.

The randomly chosen person in this study regularly wears business casual attire has driven tractors before.

What is the likelihood that the chosen participant is an office workers?
How confident do you feel about your previous likelihood rating?

In this study, we tested 500 urban residents and 500 rural residents.

The randomly chosen person in the study lives in a small yet overpriced apartment with minimal space, and drives a pickup truck whose tiers are well-equipped for all terrains.

What is the likelihood that the chosen participant is an urban resident?
How confident do you feel about your previous likelihood rating?

The randomly chosen person in the study follows a strict diet without refined sugars, often discourages people from eating fast food, and organizes events like book clubs and reading programs.

What is the likelihood that the chosen participant is a gym trainer?
How confident do you feel about your previous likelihood rating?

The randomly chosen person in the study is highly empathetic, a great storyteller, drives a luxury car to work, and has a rolex.

What is the likelihood that the chosen participant is a kindergarten teacher?
How confident do you feel about your previous likelihood rating?

The randomly chosen person in the study often talks to friends about the importance of oral hygiene for overall health, and is frequently seen wearing flashy and revealing outfits

What is the likelihood that the chosen participant is a dentist?
How confident do you feel about your previous likelihood rating?

The randomly chosen person in the study aspires to master several computer coding languages and aspires to work in the sports industry after graduation.

What is the likelihood that the chosen participant is a computer science major?
How confident do you feel about your previous likelihood rating?

What is the likelihood that the chosen participant is military personnel?
How confident do you feel about your previous likelihood rating?

Noah Goodman, PhD, Department of Psychology, Stanford University, Building 420, 450 Jane Stanford Way, Stanford, CA 94305. Phone: (650) 725-2400.

You are invited to participate in a research study about how well automated computer tools can summarise published psychology studies. You will be asked to read short descriptions of people and answer 36 questions about how likely certain statements are and how confident you feel. There are no right or wrong answers and we are interested in your own view.

The purpose of this research is to check how accurately automated computer tools can summarise published psychology studies. We are re-asking questions taken from a previously published study so that we can compare the answers with the original study's results.
You must be 18 or older to take part in this study.
Participation in this research is voluntary, and you are free to withdraw your consent at any time.
